domain.description: High-availability replication, event loops, quorum consensus, and horizontal database sharding.

domainCoverage.synopsis: In distributed systems, networks are asynchronous, packet loss is normal, and clocks drift. This volume establishes the mental models from node replication and quorum to fault isolation.

chapters.title: TCP/IP & Linux Socket Networking Internals
chapters.summary: TCP delivers an in-order, guaranteed byte stream across unreliable packet-switched IP networks. The Linux kernel manages this via send/receive socket buffers (SO_SNDBUF/SO_RCVBUF), sliding-window flow control to protect receivers from saturation, and congestion algorithms (CUBIC/BBR) to regulate transmission across shared bottlenecks.

chapters.title: Reverse Proxy Patterns & Edge Load Balancing
chapters.summary: A reverse proxy acts as an intermediary gateway positioned between external clients and private backend services. It terminates client TLS handshakes, multiplexes requests across persistent upstream connection pools, distributes traffic via balancing algorithms (Round Robin, Least Connections, P2C), and guards internal services against direct internet exposure.

chapters.title: In-Memory Caching & Event Loop Architecture
chapters.summary: Caching stores high-frequency read data in fast RAM instead of slow disk/network databases. Redis achieves sub-millisecond QPS by operating a single-threaded event loop paired with OS epoll I/O multiplexing, completely eliminating thread locking contention.

chapters.title: CDN Architecture & Geo-Distributed Edge Caching
chapters.summary: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a globally distributed network of Points of Presence (PoPs) that terminates client TCP/TLS connections physically close to users via BGP Anycast routing. By serving cached static assets and API responses from the network edge, CDNs reduce origin server load by 80-95% and drop round-trip times from hundreds of milliseconds to under 15ms.

chapters.title: Consistent Hashing
chapters.summary: Consistent Hashing is a foundational topic in Distributed Systems & Storage. Engineers use it to make predictable trade-offs under load, failure, and evolving requirements.

chapters.title: Database Sharding & Range Partitioning
chapters.summary: Sharding splits a monolithic database into independent database nodes (shards). Each row is routed to a shard based on a shard key.

chapters.title: Quorum Consistency & Raft Consensus
chapters.summary: Distributed databases replicate data across N nodes for fault tolerance. Quorum math (Read Nodes + Write Nodes > Total Nodes) guarantees that any read operation overlaps with at least one node containing the latest write.

chapters.title: CAP Theorem & Consistency Models
chapters.summary: During a network partition, a distributed store cannot simultaneously provide both strong consistency and full availability; engineering chooses which guarantee to weaken and how clients observe stale reads.
